newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - March 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - March 10.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on March 10:

WASHINGTON - Two small Native American tribes that donated $107,000 to the Democratic National Committee last year say they have faced pressure to donate even more money and hire high-profile consultants with close ties to the White House.
LOS ANGELES - Another prominent rap star -- the Notorious B.I.G. or Biggie Smalls -- was killed in a shooting that bore similarity to the drive-by shooting of Tupac Shakur six months ago.

WASHINGTON - The District of Columbia's Medicaid chief says he was directed to pay a health maintenance organization with ties to Mayor Marion Barry $18.9 million, three times more than auditors say the company deserves.
GOMA, ZAIRE - As many as 350,000 Rwandan refugees continue the sojourn they began five months ago when war broke out between Zairian insurgents and the nation's army.
UNITED NATIONS - The U.S. Congress and the world's poor countries are on a collision course over how to restructure the United Nations, casting doubt on the possibility of far-reaching reform.
